home.lede.label: Who we are
home.lede.heading: We build schools where there were none.
home.lede.body: Sumba is a savanna island of widely scattered villages. For many families the nearest school is hours away on foot, and teachers are hard to bring in. Since 2007 we have worked with village elders, local churches and the district government to open free schools — and to keep them running.

schools.hero.label: Schools
schools.hero.heading: Fourteen schools, one island.
schools.hero.body: Each school was opened at the request of its own village, and each has different needs. Six of them are shown here.
give.hero.label: Get involved
give.hero.heading: Fund something specific.
give.hero.body: Every option below is tied to one school and one need whose progress you can follow. We send photographic and financial reporting on each.
give.corporate.heading: Companies
give.corporate.body: Long-term CSR programmes with itemised budgets, site visits and auditable annual reporting.
give.church.heading: Churches
give.church.body: Congregational partnership with one named school, including regular updates and joint visits.
give.volunteer.heading: Volunteers
give.volunteer.body: We host volunteers for teacher training and construction. All volunteers complete a child safeguarding screening process.
give.how.label: How giving works
give.how.heading: A direct transfer to the foundation.
give.how.body1: We do not yet use an online payment gateway. Giving is by bank transfer, QRIS, Wise or PayPal, straight into an account held in the name of Yayasan Harapan Sumba.
give.how.body2: After transferring, send us the receipt and you will have a formal acknowledgement within three working days, along with the name of the school your gift went to.
give.tiers.heading: Six ways to give, each tied to one need.
give.ways.heading: Whichever fits how you work.
give.how.status: Information and redirect — not a payment gateway.
about.hero.label: About us
about.hero.heading: It started with one classroom under a tin roof.
about.hero.body: In 2007, seven children gathered under a tin roof in Karuni because the nearest school was a three-hour walk away. Today fourteen schools and children's homes run across the island.
about.hero.image_alt: Photograph: the first classroom at Karuni, tin roof and open walls, pupils at their desks
about.story.label: Our story
about.story.heading: Nineteen years, one village at a time.
about.story.body1: The second school came three years later, in the next valley, because an elder walked to Karuni to ask for one. Every school since has started the same way: a request from the village itself, land given by the community, and a teacher who already lives there.
about.story.body2: Nineteen years on, fourteen schools and two children's homes run across Sumba, all of them free to attend. The work is funded by foundations, churches and companies who commit for years rather than months.
about.founder.label: Founder
about.founder.heading: Reynold
about.founder.body: Reynold was born and raised in Sumba. He came back after finishing his studies with one simple conviction: the children in his village are as capable as children anywhere, and what they need is an open door.
about.founder.image_alt: Photograph: environmental portrait of Reynold in the yard of the first school
about.mission.label: Mission & vision
about.mission.heading: Free, good education, close to home.
about.mission.body: We open and run schools in underserved villages, staffed by teachers who live in those villages, at no cost to families.
about.vision.heading: A Sumba that educates its own children.
about.vision.body: Every school is designed to one day be run entirely by teachers and leaders from Sumba. Several of our first graduates now teach in the classrooms where they studied.
about.people.label: Our people
about.people.heading: The work is done by people from the island.
about.people.reynold_alt: Photograph: environmental portrait of Reynold outside the foundation office
about.people.maria: Maria Bulu — Head Teacher, SMP Harapan Anakalang

about.people.yohanis_alt: Photograph: environmental portrait of Yohanis Rangga at work on a classroom frame
about.quote.body: I want my pupils to know that from this small village, they can become anything.
homes.hero.label: Children's homes
homes.hero.heading: A home, not an institution.
homes.hero.body: Our two children's homes care for children who cannot live with their families. Each home is run by a resident house family who live alongside the children year-round.
homes.hero.image_alt: Photograph: the veranda of the house at the end of the school day, no identifiable faces
homes.care.label: Our care model
homes.care.heading: One family, not a staff rota.
homes.care.body: Children live in small groups with one permanent house family, attend the local school alongside other village children, and stay in contact with relatives wherever that is possible. The goal is always stable, long-term care.
homes.care.image_alt: Photograph: the house kitchen at the shared evening meal, no identifiable faces
homes.privacy.label: Children's privacy
homes.privacy.heading: Children in our homes are never named on this site.
homes.privacy.body: A child's family circumstances are their own private information, not ours, and not fundraising material. We tell the story of this work through the house parents, through daily life, and through young adults who have grown up and chosen to speak for themselves.

safeguarding.hero.label: Child safeguarding
safeguarding.hero.heading: How we protect the children on this site.
safeguarding.hero.body: We work with children. How we show them on the internet is therefore governed by written rules, not by habit.
safeguarding.hero.image_alt: Photograph: the printed safeguarding policy on the school noticeboard
safeguarding.rules.heading: Our rules
safeguarding.rules.body1: Children are referred to by first name only. We never publish a child's family name, and we never combine a child's name with a specific location and a daily routine.
safeguarding.rules.body2: Every photograph of a child requires written consent from a parent or guardian, and the child's own assent, specifically for use on the website. Consent for a printed newsletter is not consent for the internet.
safeguarding.rules.body3: Location data is stripped from every photograph before upload. Children living in our homes are never named, and we never explain why a child is in our care.
safeguarding.rules.body4: Consent can be withdrawn at any time. If a family asks, their child's photographs and story come off this site the same day.
safeguarding.removal.heading: Requesting removal
safeguarding.removal.body: If you are a parent, guardian, or a young person we have featured, and you want an image or story removed, contact us. You do not need to give a reason.
